arxiv-2106-03431.title: Bridge Simulation and Metric Estimation on Lie Groups
arxiv-2106-03431.creator: Mathias Højgaard Jensen, Sarang Joshi, Stefan Sommer
arxiv-2106-03431.description: Abstract We present a simulation scheme for simulating Brownian bridges on complete and connected Lie groups. We show how this simulation scheme leads to absolute continuity of the Brownian bridge measure with respect to the guided process measure. This result generalizes the Euclidean result of Delyon and Hu to Lie groups.

arxiv-2205-12143.title: Flexible Bayesian Support Vector Machines for Brain Network-based Classification
arxiv-2205-12143.creator: Jin Ming, Suprateek Kundu
arxiv-2205-12143.description: Abstract Objective : Brain networks have gained increasing recognition as potential biomarkers in mental health studies, but there are limited approaches that can leverage complex brain networks for accurate classification. Our goal is to develop a novel Bayesian Support Vector Machine (SVM) approach that incorporates high-dimensional networks as covariates and is able to overcome limitations of existing penalized methods.

arxiv-2211-02512.title: On some collinear configurations in the planar three-body problem
arxiv-2211-02512.creator: Alexei Tsygvintsev
arxiv-2211-02512.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Alexei Tsygvintsev. In this paper, we further investigate the planar Newtonian three-body problem with a focus on collinear configurations, where either the three bodies or their velocities are aligned. We provide an independent proof of Montgomery’s result [ 6 ] , stating that apart from the Lagrange’s solution, all negative energy solutions to the zero angular momentum case result in syzygies, i.e., collinear configurations of positions.

arxiv-2307-12584.title: Identifying the discs, bulges, and intra-halo light of simulated galaxies through structural decomposition 2023 Identifying the discs, bulges, and intra-halo light of simulated galaxies through structural decomposition – References
arxiv-2307-12584.creator: Katy L. Proctor, Claudia del P. Lagos, Aaron D. Ludlow Aaron S. G. Robotham
arxiv-2307-12584.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Katy L. Proctor, Claudia del P. Lagos, Aaron D. Ludlow Aaron S. G. Robotham. We perform a structural decomposition of galaxies identified in three cosmological hydrodynamical simulations by applying Gaussian Mixture Models (GMMs) to the kinematics of their stellar particles. We study the resulting disc, bulge, and intra-halo light (IHL) components of galaxies whose host dark matter haloes have virial masses in the range M 200 = 10 11 M_{200}=10^{11} – 10 15 ​ M ⊙ 10^{15}\,{\rm M_{\odot}} .

arxiv-2401-09574.title: Towards Scalable and Robust Model Versioning
arxiv-2401-09574.creator: Wenxin Ding, Arjun Nitin Bhagoji, Ben Y. Zhao, Haitao Zheng
arxiv-2401-09574.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Wenxin Ding, Arjun Nitin Bhagoji, Ben Y. Zhao, Haitao Zheng. As the deployment of deep learning models continues to expand across industries, the threat of malicious incursions aimed at gaining access to these deployed models is on the rise.

arxiv-2406-02217.title: Enhancing the sensitivity of quantum fiber-optical gyroscopes via a non-Gaussian-state probe
arxiv-2406-02217.creator: Wen-Xun Zhang, Rui Zhang, Yunlan Zuo, Le-Man Kuang
arxiv-2406-02217.description: Abstract We propose a theoretical scheme to enhance the sensitivity of a quantum fiber-optical gyroscope (QFOG) via a non-Gaussian-state probe based on quadrature measurements of the optical field. The non-Gaussian-state probe utilizes the product state comprising a photon-added coherent state (PACS) with photon excitations and a coherent state CS.

arxiv-2411-07522.title: Protected chaos in a topological lattice
arxiv-2411-07522.creator: Haydar Sahin, Hakan Akgün, Zhuo Bin Siu, S. M. Rafi-Ul-Islam, Jian Feng Kong, Mansoor B. A. Jalil, Ching Hua Lee
arxiv-2411-07522.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Haydar Sahin, Hakan Akgün, Zhuo Bin Siu, S. M. Rafi-Ul-Islam, Jian Feng Kong, Mansoor B. A. Jalil, Ching Hua Lee. Published version —Adv. https://doi.org/10.1002/advs.202503216 Keywords — protected chaos, non-linear topology, topological protection, machine learning The erratic nature of chaotic behavior is thought to erode the stability of periodic behavior, including topological oscillations. However, we discover that in the presence of chaos, non-trivial topology not only endures but also provides robust protection to chaotic dynamics within a topological lattice hosting non-linear oscillators.

arxiv-2502-01712.title: Summing large Pomeron loops in the saturation region: dipole-nucleus collision beyond nonlinear equations.
arxiv-2502-01712.creator: Eugene Levin
arxiv-2502-01712.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Eugene Levin. In this paper we found the dipole-nucleus scattering amplitude at high energies by summing large Pomeron loops. It turns out that the energy dependence of this amplitude is the same as for dipole-dipole scattering.

arxiv-2503-13394.title: On the formation of the 1 : 2 1:2 resonance in oscillator dynamics
arxiv-2503-13394.creator: Jan Kyzioł, Andrzej Okniński
arxiv-2503-13394.description: Abstract The dynamics of nonlinear oscillators are investigated. We study the formation of 1 : 2 1:2 resonance in nonlinear periodically forced oscillators due to period doubling of the primary 1 : 1 1:1 resonance, or born independently. We compute the amplitude-frequency implicit function, the steady-state asymptotic solution, for the effective equation approximating coupled oscillators.

arxiv-2512-04521.title: WiFi-based Cross-Domain Gesture Recognition Using Attention Mechanism Thanks: Ruijing Liu, Cunhua Pan, jiaming Zeng, Hong Ren are with the National Mobile Communications Research Laboratory, Southeast University, Nanjing 210096, China (e-mail: 230258158@seu.edu.cn; cpan@seu.edu.cn; 220250992@seu.edu
arxiv-2512-04521.creator: Ruijing Liu, Cunhua Pan, Jiaming Zeng, Hong Ren
arxiv-2512-04521.description: Abstract While fulfilling communication tasks, wireless signals can also be used to sense the environment. Among various types of sensing media, WiFi signals offer advantages such as widespread availability, low hardware cost, and strong robustness to environmental conditions like light, temperature, and humidity.

pmc-10483270.creator: Wei Li, Yan Wang, Fan Liu, Haijiao Xie, Hui Yin, Tian Yi
pmc-10483270.description: Various exotic metal cations commonly coexist with ferrihydrite nanoparticles in natural environments. Lack of knowledge about the metal cations effects on ferrihydrite nucleation and growth greatly blights the deep understanding of ferrihydrite mineralogical properties and reactivities, and thus the fates of associated nutrients, heavy metals/metalloids, and organic pollutants.

pmc-10542609.title: Altitude, latitude and climate zone as determinants of mountain hare (Lepus timidus) coat colour change
pmc-10542609.creator: Allan W Stokes, Tim R Hofmeester, Neri H Thorsen, John Odden, John D C Linnell, Simen Pedersen
pmc-10542609.description: Local adaptation to annually changing environments has evolved in numerous species. Seasonal coat colour change is an adaptation that has evolved in multiple mammal and bird species occupying areas that experience seasonal snow cover. It has a critical impact on fitness as predation risk may increase when an individual is mismatched against its habitat's background colour.

pmc-10649119.title: Preparation of COPs Mixed Matrix Membrane for Sensitive Determination of Six Sulfonamides in Human Urine
pmc-10649119.creator: Ying Liu, Yong Zhang, Jing Wang, Kexin Wang, Shuming Gao, Ruiqi Cui, Fubin Liu, Guihua Gao
pmc-10649119.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). In this study, TpDMB-COPs, a specific class of covalent organic polymers (COPs), was synthesized using Schiff-base chemistry and incorporated into a polyvinylidene fluoride (PVDF) polymer for the first time to prepare COPs mixed matrix membranes (TpDMB-COPs-MMM). A membrane solid-phase extraction (ME) method based on the TpDMB-COPs-MMM was developed to extract trace levels of six sulfonamides from human urine identified by high-performance liquid chromatography (HPLC). The key factors affecting the extraction efficiency were investigated.

pmc-10738431.title: DEVELOPMENT OF THE LONGITUDINAL STUDY OF HEALTH AND AGEING IN KENYA (LOSHAK)
pmc-10738431.creator: Niranjani Nagarajan, Joshua Ehrlich, Anthony Ngugi, Eunice Mwangi, Roselyter Riang’a, Shaheen Sayed, Muthoni Gichu, Kenneth Langa
pmc-10738431.description: In Kenya, the number of adults aged ≥60 is expected to nearly quadruple by 2050, making it one of the most rapidly aging countries in Sub-Saharan Africa (SSA). Accordingly, we designed the Longitudinal Study of Health and Ageing in Kenya (LOSHAK) to generate novel data to address the health and economic consequences of this demographic transition. Modeled on the U.S.

pmc-12612746.title: Prevalence of obsessive-compulsive disorder and related healthcare utilisation in China: a cross-sectional epidemiological survey
pmc-12612746.creator: Bangshan Liu, Junzhe Cheng, Zhaorui Liu, Yueqin Huang, Shazia Rehman, Minxue Shen, Jin Liu, Yumeng Ju, Yaqin Yu, Xiufeng Xu, Zhizhong Wang, Yifeng Xu, Tao Li, Guangming Xu, Xiangdong Xu, Limin Wang, Yongping Yan, Shuiyuan Xiao, Tingting Zhang, Jie Yan, Lingjiang Li, Huifang Yin, Yan Zhang
pmc-12612746.description: BackgroundObsessive-compulsive disorder (OCD) is classified by the World Health Organization as 1 of the 10 most disabling conditions. However, nationally representative epidemiological data on OCD are not yet available in China.AimsTo investigate the prevalence, comorbidity, role impairment and healthcare utilisation of OCD in China.

pmc-12635662.title: Evaluation of pancreatic adenocarcinoma with tumor budding and lymphocytic infiltration as prognostic marker
pmc-12635662.creator: Sunil V Jagtap, Shubham S Jagtap
pmc-12635662.description: Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) is the most prevalent type of pancreatic neoplasm. It is a highly aggressive lethal malignancy related to its delayed in diagnosis and limited response to treatments. The incidence and mortality of pancreatic cancer have been increasing over the years. Tumor budding is a proven independent, adverse prognostic factor in PDAC.

pmc-13240418.title: Derivation and Pluripotency Validation of Six iPSC Lines From Amniotic Fluid Carrying Intermediate α‐Thalassemia Genotypes (‐‐3.7/αSEA and ‐‐4.2/αSEA)
pmc-13240418.creator: Qingyun Chen, Xinxing Jiang, Xinhuai Xue, Yao Zhou, Yuanhua Huang, Fei Sun, Yanlin Ma, Harleen Khatra
pmc-13240418.description: PurposeThalassemia intermedia (TI), or hemoglobin H (Hb H) disease, presents significant clinical heterogeneity, and its pathogenesis remains unclear. This study aimed to establish induced pluripotent stem cells (iPSCs) from amniotic fluid (AF) cells of fetuses diagnosed with intermediate α‐thalassemia genotypes (‐α3.7/‐‐SEA and ‐α4.2/‐‐SEA) to provide a robust in vitro model for investigating disease mechanisms and exploring therapeutic strategies.

pmc-13283200.title: Triglyceride-Glucose Index and Mortality Risk in the General Population: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis of Prospective Studies
pmc-13283200.creator: D’Elia Lanfranco, Saverio Stranges, Ersilia La Fata, Francesca Fortunato, Raffaele Palladino, Domenico Rendina, Ferruccio Galletti
pmc-13283200.description: IntroductionInsulin resistance (IR) is a major determinant of cardiovascular disease and mortality, yet its direct measurement is limited by the need for insulin assays. The triglyceride–glucose (TyG) index has emerged as a simple and inexpensive surrogate marker of IR, but its prognostic relevance for mortality remains uncertain due to the heterogeneity of available studies.

pmc-13430363.creator: Bingjie Ye, Chengfu Xu
pmc-13430363.description: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) has emerged as the most prevalent chronic liver disease worldwide and is closely linked to systemic metabolic disorders. In addition to their classical role in hemostasis, platelets are increasingly recognized as active regulators of inflammation and immune responses, yet their contribution to MASLD pathogenesis remains incompletely defined.
